clue.text: Humourless dandy in recession unable to retrieve service

indicators.note: going into recession means moving back, so the word for dandy is read backwards

parts.note: a fop is a vain, overdressed man, a dandy
in tennis a player who cannot return a serve has been aced

explanation.surface: A humourless fop, now broke, fails to get the waiter's attention back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns FOP into POF; 'service' looks like restaurant service, but it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Po-faced describes someone with a solemn, disapproving expression, without humour.

clue.text: Aggressive, feeble companion arrested

indicators.note: arrested means held, so one piece is caught inside the other

parts.note: puny means weak or feeble
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A weak friend has been taken into custody, which seems a bit violent.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchy means forceful or aggressive in style.

clue.text: Infer object is a fireside frame

indicators.note: read as a separate word, In says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the letters of Infer after its first two
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Deduce that the thing is a fireplace guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infer' looks like a verb meaning deduce, but it splits as 'In fer', with 'In' signalling the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a low metal frame in front of a fireplace.

clue.text: Black singer maintaining tenor arrangement is repellent

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the singer's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Cilla Black was a popular British singer and TV presenter

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word puts its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A black vocalist keeps a tenor's musical arrangement, which is off-putting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' is not a colour but a surname: Cilla Black, a 1960s British pop singer. 'arrangement' scrambles the voice type before it goes inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Citronella oil is used as an insect repellent.

clue.text: Reportedly the first W in genetic engineering?

definitions.text: Reportedly the first W in genetic engineering?

parts.words: Reportedly the first W in genetic engineering?
parts.note: W said out loud is double-you, and a clone is a double of you; the first female sheep, said like the letter U, cloned by scientists

explanation.definitionFit: This was the famous ewe cloned in Scotland in 1996, the first mammal copied from an adult cell.

clue.text: Serious money

definitions.meaning: as in a ... offence, one grave enough to carry the death penalty
wealth or funds used to start or run a business

explanation.definitionFit: Capital means grave (a capital crime) and also funds invested in business.

clue.text: One's fried in oil when flirt embraces king

indicators.note: embraces means hugs, so the word for flirt surrounds the king

parts.note: a coquette is a flirtatious woman
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A flirt hugs a monarch while something sizzles in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small cake of mashed food coated in breadcrumbs and deep-fried.

clue.text: Look for little sound

definitions.meaning: a ... is a faint squeak, as in not a ... out of you

explanation.definitionFit: Peep means a quick glance and also a tiny noise.

clue.text: See 4
Late dispatch sounded at late dispatch?

definitions.meaning: the final mail collection of the day
the bugle call played at military funerals, when the late person is sent off

explanation.definitionFit: The Last Post is both the day's final mail and the bugle call played at funerals.

clue.text: Group of ten, one taken away

definitions.text: Group of ten, one taken away

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ten-strong band loses a member.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'away' cannot define the answer; the whole clue does: a group of ten with one taken away is a group of nine, and the letters sit in teN ONE Taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine musicians, which is what ten becomes when one leaves.

clue.text: John senses abnormal laxity

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: something abnormal is out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named John has unusual perceptions about slackness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is slang for a toilet; 'abnormal' rearranges SENSES into SENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Looseness and laxity both mean slackness or a lack of strictness.

clue.text: His cherubs depicted cheekily, upsetting his moony cherubs

indicators.note: upsetting the words knocks their letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter's impish cherubs are shown in a way that offends his dreamy angels.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of 'his moony cherubs' are rearranged by 'upsetting'; the painter's busy hellscapes are full of mischievous little figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch painter filled his crowded scenes with strange, impish figures, so his cherubs are depicted with cheek.

clue.text: Hack gets the sack

definitions.meaning: to hack is to cut roughly, as with an axe
getting the ... means being dismissed from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Chop means to cut roughly, and 'the chop' is dismissal from work.

clue.text: Doctor admits this setter's pudding, but I'll go down fighting!

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the doctor's letters surround the rest

parts.note: the setter speaking says I have, contracted to I've
a bombe is a dome-shaped frozen dessert

explanation.surface: A doctor lets in the setter's dessert, which goes down defiantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll go down fighting!' looks like a defiant cry, but describes a plane that dives to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive-bomber is a warplane that plunges steeply towards its target to attack it.

clue.text: Massive stirrers stick with sociable people

parts.note: to cement is to stick things together
good mixers are people who socialise easily

explanation.surface: Glue together with party-goers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement mixers are big rotating drums that stir concrete, so they are huge stirrers.

clue.text: Having dismissed Australian opener, incredibly certain six is not involved

indicators.note: incredibly signals an unbelievable rearrangement of the letters
having dismissed means sending away, so a letter is removed
the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: After the Aussie opening batsman is out, the cricket match has six runs that don't count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having dismissed' takes A (Australian opener) out of CERTAIN, leaving CERTIN; 'incredibly' rearranges that with SIX. Dismissing an opener is a cricket picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic means coming from outside, not part of the essential nature of something.

clue.text: When our secret troops are bad, one kills

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
the SAS is the British Special Air Service, a secretive military unit
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Even our covert soldiers do wrong when one of them is a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: SAS is Britain's special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is one who kills, typically a prominent person.

clue.text: Help one to get better, given disadvantage

parts.note: a hand is help, as in lend a hand
I is the Roman numeral one
to cap is to outdo or better

explanation.surface: Helping someone recover, despite a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get better' looks like recovering, but means to cap, to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a hindrance, something that puts one at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Always after a winter warmer, Grant lodged a complaint

indicators.note: after places the word for always behind the rest
lodged means placed inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a scarf keeps the neck warm in winter
to let is to allow or grant
ever is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A man called Grant, wearing a scarf, has a constant grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a surname but is a verb meaning allow; 'lodged' sets it inside the winter garment and 'after' puts the word for always at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever is an infectious illness, and a complaint is an illness.

clue.text: Overtake on motorway, reversing here and there

parts.note: to pass a car is to overtake it

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the motorway letters run backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A driver passes on the motorway and then backs up, all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, London to Leeds, is the UK's first long motorway; 'reversing' turns MI into IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin used in references to mean found throughout, here and there.

clue.text: Dash into dress-rehearsal, say

definitions.meaning: a short horizontal line in writing
the mark that goes into a compound such as dress-rehearsal

explanation.definitionFit: A hyphen is a dash-like mark, the one joining dress and rehearsal.

clue.text: Supporter of a fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: A fan of a certain fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant, someone who supports another in their work.

clue.text: Religious figure often hailed to safeguard one's religious nation — such as I?

indicators.note: to safeguard is to hold protectively, so one word surrounds the others

parts.note: the Virgin Mary is greeted in the Hail Mary prayer
one is I and 's stands for is
Sion, or Zion, is the Jewish people or homeland in religious terms

explanation.surface: A holy figure guards her faithful nation, and the speaker claims to be one too.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Paul, and St Paul was the great early evangelist, so 'such as I?' defines the answer. 'Religious figure' looks like the definition but is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's pseudonym is Paul, and the apostle Paul travelled spreading the faith, the model of a preacher abroad.

clue.text: Stitch up with thread?

definitions.meaning: a threaded fastener driven into wood or metal

explanation.definitionFit: Screw means to cheat someone and also a threaded metal fastener.

clue.text: Source of sugar cane, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is one that sounds alike

parts.note: to cane is to beat with a stick

explanation.surface: Sugar cane gets a mention as the origin of sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sugar cane' looks like one thing, but cane is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is a root crop from which much of the world's sugar is refined.

clue.text: One in pursuit of Croesus's cash remains missing, mysteriously

indicators.note: mysteriously means the letters are mixed up in a puzzling way

parts.note: the name Croesus with the possessive S kept as a letter

indicators.note: missing means the word for remains is left out of cash

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Someone after a fabulously rich king's money finds what's left has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes ASH out of CASH, leaving C; 'mysteriously' rearranges that with CROESUSS. Croesus was a proverbially wealthy king of Lydia.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is one who follows after another, coming in pursuit of them.

clue.text: See 11
Writer turns from the listener in favour of family

indicators.note: turns means the word for writer is turned round

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
otic means relating to the ear, the listener's organ

explanation.surface: An author changes course and starts favouring relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses PEN to NEP. 'listener' looks like a person but is the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotic describes nepotism, giving jobs or favours to relatives.

clue.text: Know moves with arm and hand

indicators.note: moves means the letters shift into another order

explanation.surface: Learn exercises with arm and hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges KNOW and ARM; 'hand' looks like part of the body, but means a worker, as in farmhand.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual labourer, as in factory hand, so it can mean a worker.
